title: Contest Problem Provenance Trail
whatYouGet: A provenance investigation that separates exact-source evidence, likely relatives and unsourced lookalikes.
howToUse: Paste the complete problem and any claimed citation, then inspect AoPS threads and original-source evidence manually.
effectiveUsage: 1. Paste the problem character-for-character with any attribution.
2. Extract distinctive non-numeric phrases and structural features.
3. Open the AoPS search and inspect source notes inside matching threads.
4. Record a contest attribution only when an inspectable primary or credible secondary source supports it.
commonFix: If wrong, reply with: "Remove unsupported contest claims, distinguish exact matches from variants and show the evidence chain for every attribution."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a competition-problem provenance researcher and evidence-chain editor.

CONTEXT: A teacher has [PROBLEM TEXT] described as [CLAIMED SOURCE] and needs to know whether the attribution is supportable.

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [PROBLEM TEXT]
- [CLAIMED SOURCE]
- [LANGUAGE OR TRANSLATION HISTORY]
- [KNOWN VARIANTS]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:
- [AOPS] Whitelist: https://artofproblemsolving.com/community/q1_{ENCODED_KEYWORDS}. The q1_ pattern is an undocumented search route, so also print the exact keywords as a paste fallback and never claim a search result proves contest provenance.
- [MATH_STACKEXCHANGE] Whitelist: https://math.stackexchange.com/search?q={ENCODED_KEYWORDS}. Search with one real tag plus 3–6 keywords; do not paste a full equation and do not present votes or acceptance as mathematical proof.

DO THIS:
1. Extract distinctive keywords, theorem structure and unusual constants without pasting the full equation into a query.
2. Build an AoPS q1_ keyword search and a Math StackExchange search when conceptual relatives may help.
3. Classify hits as exact text, mathematical equivalent, inspired variant or unrelated lookalike.
4. Record the contest, year and problem number only when the opened thread supplies traceable evidence.
5. Prefer an official paper or archive over a forum assertion when one is available.
6. Return UNSOURCED when the chain remains incomplete.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Search for the provenance of a quadratic inequality olympiad problem.
Expected result or check target: The teacher gets a focused AoPS results page and must inspect matching threads for an actual citation.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://artofproblemsolving.com/community/q1_quadratic%20inequality%20olympiad%20source
(paste-fallback: quadratic inequality olympiad source)
Encoding note: AoPS search spaces use %20; the decoded q1_ keywords match the fallback exactly.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Problem Fingerprint — distinctive words and mathematical structure
2. Search Trail — AoPS and supporting human-source routes
3. Match Table — exact, equivalent, variant or unrelated
4. Attribution Verdict — supported, probable or unsourced
5. Citation Record — evidence the teacher actually inspected

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Never turn a familiar-looking problem into a claimed PYQ or olympiad citation.
- AoPS threads are human evidence leads; they do not prove attribution without inspectable source details.
- Do not invent years, problem numbers, authors, scans or URLs.
- Use MathOverflow only for research-history questions, not contest-source lookup.
- Preserve the exact supplied problem while comparing variants.
- Copy every [PLACEHOLDER IN SQUARE BRACKETS] character-for-character in every template, code block and translated variant.
- Never output a desmos.com URL with parameters, a mathsolver.microsoft.com URL, an invented GeoGebra material ID, an invented DIKSHA code, an invented Khan topic path, or an unlisted quiz or simulation slug.

   (Forms only with entry.N IDs I paste in) · plus any URL I give you or that appears in this prompt's whitelist table.
